key_insight: The paper argues that future interactive world models should be treated less like frame-predicting video generators and more like game engines that maintain state, rules, and long-term consistency. This shift enables interactions to produce coherent outcomes as the world evolves, not just visually plausible next frames.
problem_solved: It addresses the gap between current video generative models and truly interactive worlds: existing models can predict observations from actions, but they often fail to enforce persistent game state and rule-based behavior over time.
method: Reframe interactive world modeling as a stateful engine problem rather than purely pixel prediction.
Condition future predictions on user actions while tracking evolving world conditions and rules.
Emphasize interaction outcomes that remain coherent across time, supporting longer-horizon consistency in dynamic environments.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a clearer design target for building interactive simulations, agents, and game-like environments that behave consistently under user control. It can improve research in generative world models, embodied AI, and controllable content generation.
visual_elements: Before/after diagram comparing pixel-only prediction vs state-based game engine modeling

Timeline illustrating how consistency evolves across multiple user interactions

paper_title: From Pixels to States: Rethinking Interactive World Models as Game Engines
paper_authors: Zhen Li, Zian Meng, Shuwei Shi, Mingliang Zhai, Jiaming Tan
